interpretations: Each line below is one distinct reading of the question

Observatory stations are taken only from `telescopes`, so only stations with at least one telescope count. Share = count / total rows in `telescopes`. The average share is the mean of those shares (equal to 1/number of stations with telescopes). Keep stations with a share strictly above the average, take the top 10 by share minus average descending, and show the share as a fraction
The same as 1, but the average share is 1/number of all rows in `observatories`, so stations with zero telescopes lower the average
The same as 2, but stations with zero telescopes are also listed as candidates (count 0), though they can never be above average
The same as 1, but "above the average" means greater than or equal to the average share
The same as 1, but the share and the gap are shown as percentages (multiplied by 100) rather than fractions

The same as 1, but the average is computed as the average telescope count per station, and the gap is (count − average count) / total telescopes. This gives the same ranking but is a different computation path
The same as 1, but the average share is a telescope-weighted average (sum of squared shares) rather than a simple mean across stations
The same as 1, but only telescopes that appear in `signals` (via `telescref`) are counted. The total and the average are then based on those telescopes only
The same as 1, but the telescope count is the number of distinct `telescregistry` values, with the total taken as the distinct telescope count
The same as 1, but ties at the 10th position are all included, so more than 10 rows may be returned
The same as 1, but ties at the 10th position are broken arbitrarily or by `observstation` alphabetical order, returning exactly 10 rows
The same as 1, but the average is taken over only the top-ranked or above-average stations rather than all stations
The same as 1, but the output also shows the average share as a constant column alongside `observstation`, count, share and gap
The same as 1, but the station name is taken from `observatories.observstation` joined to `telescopes`, with whitespace or padding differences (CHAR(60)) trimmed before grouping
queries:
SELECT observstation,
       CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telescopes) AS share
FROM telescopes
GROUP BY observstation
HAVING CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telescopes) >
       (SELECT 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT observstation) FROM telescopes)
ORDER BY CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telescopes) -
         (SELECT 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT observstation) FROM telescopes) DESC
LIMIT 10;
SELECT t.observstation
FROM telescopes t
GROUP BY t.observstation
HAVING COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telescopes) > 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM observatories);
SELECT o.observstation
FROM observatories o
LEFT JOIN telescopes t ON t.observstation = o.observstation
GROUP BY o.observstation
HAVING COUNT(t.telescregistry) > (SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM observatories) FROM telescopes);
